newsitem.title: USA: Yellow raises general freight rate.
newsitem.headline: Yellow raises general freight rate.

text.p: Yellow Freight System said Wednesday it will raise its general freight rate an average of 5.2 percent effective January 1, 1997.

Yellow Freight, a subsidiary of Yellow Corp, said the increased rate reflects the investments it has made to enhance customer service and other less-than-truckload (LTL) transportation solutions it offers.

"Yellow has worked to increase the customer value of these services, all while creating a more efficient organization," Yellow Freight President Bill Zollars said in a statement. "However, in order for us to continue delivering the level of service and enabling technology that has become an expectation, we must implement this rate increase."

Yellow Freight said it has invested more than $70 million in new technology in the past few years, including in its customer service center. It added that its customers have placed a priority on supply chain management and reducing inventory carrying expenses.
Yellow Freight said it is continuing to address those issues through a number of programs that allow freight information to move ahead of the actual freight.
The company said the general rate increase will be independent from a fuel surcharge that it implemented in September.

"Fuel and labor costs are two of our biggest expenses," Zollars said. "We will continue to closely monitor all costs, and if fuel costs moderate, the surcharge will be adjusted or dropped accordingly."
In addition to the general rate increase, Yellow said it is enacting two transaction charges. Beginning January 1, 1997, Yellow will begin charging $10 for each reversal of freight charges.

Also beginning January 1, a $10 charge will be levied to adjust freight to proper weight and classification on the freight bill. A $10 bill fee will be applied to the freight bill when an error in weight or classification occurs and the result adds $20 or more to the cost of moving the freight.
